title: What Killed Liberalism?
gist: Subscriber-exclusive teaser: Gene Frieda reviews new books by Gordon Brown and Daron Acemoglu on liberalism's decline, arguing a single culprit is futile to seek and the real question is rebuilding institutions that gave people community and agency; notes the postwar order giving way to spheres of influence as tariffs and sanctions are weaponized.

insights.claim: Modern liberal democracy is buckling in many countries, with established parties shedding support and populist movements moving from the fringes into the political mainstream.
insights.speaker: GENE FRIEDA
insights.so_what: Mainstream populism raises policy unpredictability and political risk premia in developed markets.
insights.quote: Modern liberal democracy is buckling in many countries whose citizens have known no other system

insights.claim: Searching for a single culprit behind liberalism's decline is probably futile; the harder and more useful question is how to rebuild the institutions that once gave people a sense of community and power over their lives.
insights.speaker: GENE FRIEDA
insights.so_what: Points to institution-rebuilding policy agendas (community, local power) as the likely response, rather than quick fixes.
insights.quote: searching for a single culprit is probably futile
insights.locator: There is no shortage of people

themes.theme: From liberal order to spheres of influence

insights.claim: As governments weaponize tariffs and sanctions, the postwar liberal order is giving way to spheres of influence and naked exercises of raw power.
insights.speaker: GENE FRIEDA
insights.so_what: Weaponized trade tools imply persistent fragmentation, tariff risk and sanctions exposure for global supply chains and capital flows.
insights.quote: As governments weaponize tariffs and sanctions, the postwar liberal order is giving way to spheres of influence and naked exercises of raw power.
